messages:
Maya Patel: heads-up — we got a PG escalation from AcmeFinance. Their rerank results changed after last night's model push. Same query + candidates, different order and scores. Customer is seeing production regressions and is pretty upset.

Ajay Singhal: ugh. do we have their request payload and exact timestamps?

Maya Patel: pasted below. they included the original request id and sample candidate set. they say it started ~2026-02-22 03:10 UTC (which aligns w/ our v1.2 rollout).

Maya Patel: ```json
{"request_id":"acme-req-20260222-17","model":"rwr-rerank-1.2","query":"Which of these loans has the lowest APR?","candidates":["Loan A: 3.2% APR, fixed","Loan B: 2.9% APR variable","Loan C: 3.2% APR, variable"],"top_k":3}
```

Maya Patel: customer says with v1.1 they got scores [0.82, 0.79, 0.11] -> order A,B,C. After v1.2 same input returns [0.35, 0.33, 0.31] -> order A,C,B. so B & C flipped and scores collapsed.

Chris O'Neill: thanks — initial thoughts: big collapses like that could be normalization change or a different scoring head. v1.2 had a small changeset to the final dense layer and we also changed per-request score normalization to L2-prefactor (was softmax earlier?). need to confirm.

Lina Gomez: @Chris do you have the changelog link? i can diff the commit.

Chris O'Neill: changelist: https://internal/repo/models/rwr/commits/1.2 — note two things: 1) scoring head weights updated (fine-tune) and 2) introduced optional "normalize_scores": "l2" flag in the model config (default true in v1.2). v1.1 default was false.

Ajay Singhal: ok that explains magnitude collapse but not swap between B & C unless tokenization/inputs changed. are we certain customer payload didn't hit candidate truncation or reorder due to JSON parsing?

Maya Patel: customer sent the exact JSON above. they confirmed no extra whitespace. they also included raw logs (attaching):

Maya Patel: ```
[2026-02-22T03:10:12Z] POST /v1/rerank 200 req=acme-req-20260222-17 model=rwr-rerank-1.1 scores=[0.82,0.79,0.11]
[2026-02-22T03:10:12Z] POST /v1/rerank 200 req=acme-req-20260222-17 model=rwr-rerank-1.2 scores=[0.35,0.33,0.31]
```

Maya Patel: they ran both requests back-to-back against our hosted endpoint pinned to model param.

Ajay Singhal: great repro. let's reproduce locally. can someone run curl + & include debug flags? also need raw logits and tokenization.

Lina Gomez: running quick local repro: using the same code and candidate strings. small script attached.

Lina Gomez: ```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"rwr-rerank-1.1","query":"Which of these loans has the lowest APR?","candidates":["Loan A: 3.2% APR, fixed","Loan B: 2.9% APR variable","Loan C: 3.2% APR, variable"],"include_raw_scores":true}'
```

Lina Gomez: results (local): v1.1 -> raw_scores: [2.63, 2.39, -1.50] -> normalized softmax -> [0.82,0.79,0.11] as expected. v1.2 -> raw_scores: [0.12, 0.05, 0.03] -> L2-normalized -> [0.35,0.33,0.31].

Chris O'Neill: that confirms the change. raw logits changed magnitude because final layer weights changed, then model config normalization switched to L2, which compresses.

Ajay Singhal: why would B & C swap relative ordering? logits for B and C are very close in v1.2 (0.05 vs 0.03). small float noise / tokenization ties could flip order. are we doing deterministic tokenization?

Lina Gomez: tokenization identical. i diffed tokens: B tokens = [Loan, B, :, 2.9, %, APR, variable] C tokens = [Loan, C, :, 3.2, %, APR, variable]. logits close because content similar. In v1.1 difference larger likely because scoring head emphasized APR numeric tokens more. v1.2 head weight changes deemphasized them.

Maya Patel: customer says they never changed UI; they expected pinning model would avoid regressions. they did pin to model param, but were still on v1.2 after our rollout — they expected model semantics to be stable across minor versions.

Ajay Singhal: note for customers: model updates can change relative scores; we should publish semantic compatibility guidelines. For this specific escalation we need to offer mitigation: pin older model (rwr-rerank-1.1) for them, or adjust normalization flag.

Chris O'Neill: we can add an emergency deploy: set model config for v1.2 to default to "normalize_scores": "softmax" to match v1.1 behaviour as a temporary rollback of normalization. but final-layer weight diffs would still slightly change scores.

Maya Patel: customer asks for exact repro steps they can run to compare. Lina can you paste minimal reproducible commands with both models and expected outputs?

Lina Gomez: sure — commands:

1) v1.1 (pin):
```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"rwr-rerank-1.1","query":"Which of these loans has the lowest APR?","candidates":["Loan A: 3.2% APR, fixed","Loan B: 2.9% APR variable","Loan C: 3.2% APR, variable"],"include_raw_scores":true}' | jq .
```

Expected raw_scores ~ [2.6,2.4,-1.5] and normalized [0.82,0.79,0.11].

2) v1.2 (current):
```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"rwr-rerank-1.2","query":"Which of these loans has the lowest APR?","candidates":["Loan A: 3.2% APR, fixed","Loan B: 2.9% APR variable","Loan C: 3.2% APR, variable"],"include_raw_scores":true}' | jq .
```

Expected raw_scores ~ [0.12,0.05,0.03] and L2-normalized [0.35,0.33,0.31].

Ajay Singhal: action items: 1) support: offer customer immediate pin to rwr-rerank-1.1 and credit for disruption. 2) eng: assess whether v1.2 default normalization change was intended (CC: @chris). 3) eng-ml: evaluate if weight update regressed business metrics for common queries.

Chris O'Neill: confirming — normalization change was intentional for calibration experiments, but we failed to flag as breaking change. that's on me. i'll open a rollback PR to flip default back for hosted customers and mark it experimental.

Maya Patel: customer asked also if this could be due to input formatting / candidate ordering in our SDK. i've checked their SDK logs; they sent JSON array in same order. no reordering.

Lina Gomez: small note: when scores are nearly equal, downstream UI which uses tie-breaker by timestamp could also change visible order; ask customer to verify they rank strictly by score.

Maya Patel: customer insisted they sort by score desc. we provided the raw arrays above.

support-bot: Incident ticket created: INC-2026-0423 — Rerank score regression (AcmeFinance). Assigned to eng oncall.

Ajay Singhal: assigned tasks -> Lina to provide reproducible script + token diffs (in progress). Chris to PR normalization rollback. Customer contact: i'll offer pin and 2 weeks of free usage + run a quality check across 1000 customer queries to measure impact.

Maya Patel: thanks everyone. i'll send customer a clear write-up + repro steps and keep thread updated. will mark as high priority. :pray:

Chris O'Neill: quick follow-up: we should improve release notes and a changelog flag for any normalization/decoding/scoring-head changes. i'll add to eng runbook.

Maya Patel: noted. closing loop with ACME once pinned and we have monitoring check results.

(END)
